_comments: THE MONTHLY RECOGNITION PASS (D92 §8). This row is what makes post-time recognition work at all:
booking no longer stages forward-dated release entries, so without a caller on the 1st of the
month nothing recognises revenue on a subscription ever again. It is not an optimisation.
IT SHIPS DISABLED, AND THE REASON IS NOT CAUTION. This row was written Active on purpose, because
the failure it guards is doing NOTHING: the PR that adds it removes the staging that used to
recognise this revenue, so a disabled job would mean no time-driven revenue is recognised at all.
That argument still holds — but it only holds on a database that has never staged. Andrew's review
(2026-09-22) found the case it misses: a deferred line confirmed BEFORE cutover already has its
staged release entries in the ledger while its RecognizedToDate reads 0, so the first cumulative
pass would recognise the whole line a second time. Every such line, silently, in one run.
So Active is only safe after a one-time reconciliation: set RecognizedToDate from the staged
entries dated on or before cutover, and void the staged entries after it. Until that exists and a
check holds it, this job must not run — and this PR is parked, so it does not exist yet.
THE REHEARSAL IS A DRY RUN, NOT A DISABLED JOB. Before this reaches an environment that matters,
call `Orders.PostDueRecognition` with `Preview: true` and `AsOf` set to the prior month end and
read the counts — that is the same pass, over the same lines, writing nothing. It is a better
gate than a disabled schedule because it can be run deliberately, at a moment somebody is looking,
rather than depending on a person to flip two settings in the right order afterwards.
FIRST SCHEDULED RUN: 2026-10-01 02:30 UTC, with AsOf 2026-09-30.
· It is CUMULATIVE, so that first pass recognises everything owing since each line was booked,
not just September. On a database with existing subscriptions that is a large entry set and it
is correct — it is the revenue those lines had already earned and the staging had already
written forward-dated. Read the dry run before the date if that matters to the close.
02:30 UTC ON THE 1st, AHEAD OF ACCOUNTING'S 03:00 SWEEP. The sweep posts the Pending entries in the
period it is closing; this pass is what creates them. Half an hour is not a race the ordering
depends on — a late pass's entries would simply be swept the following month, dated correctly but
posted a period behind — but the close reads far better when the two run in order on the same night.
`AsOf` IS NOT CONFIGURED, deliberately. The Action defaults it to the last day of the PRIOR month,
which is the period a run on the 1st is closing. Pinning a literal date here would close the same
month forever; passing 'today' would push every month's revenue into the month after it.
MONTHLY, NOT DAILY, unlike the renewal pass. A daily run would post a dated entry every day for the
fraction earned that day, which is not how the drivers slice a period and not how a close is read.
The cumulative arithmetic means a missed month is picked up whole by the next run.
· ConcurrencyMode `Skip` — a second pass would find zero deltas and post nothing, but two passes
racing on the same line would both read the same RecognizedToDate before either wrote.
· MissedRunPolicy `RunOnce` — several missed months are one catch-up by construction.
· RunImmediatelyIfNeverRun `false` — the schedule is the close's calendar, not the deploy's. A
deployment mid-month must not post a period that is not over.
· MaxRuntimeMinutes 60 — one transaction per line across every open subscription in the book,
and the first live pass is the longest this job will ever run.
· NotifyOnFailure — a line that could not post is a line whose revenue is missing from the close.
OwnerUserID / NotifyUserID are deliberately unset: they name people, which differs per environment,
and a metadata row that asserted one would overwrite whoever the host had chosen.

fields.Name: Orders — Post Due Recognition (monthly)
fields.Description: Recognises revenue earned through the end of the prior month on every confirmed line whose revenue recognition type is deferred and time-driven, running ahead of accounting's monthly sweep. Ships ACTIVE and live: booking no longer stages release entries, so a disabled job would mean no time-driven revenue is recognised at all. Rehearse with Orders.PostDueRecognition Preview true for the prior month end. The pass is cumulative, so the first run recognises everything owing since each line was booked.
